mainTopic: Benefit and damage in one item, which הקדש items can be misused again and again (מועל אחר מועל), and how רבי differs from the תנא קמא
overview: The משנה teaches that a person only commits מעילה on an item that can be damaged if he gets a פרוטה's worth of benefit and causes a פרוטה's worth of damage to the same item. It then teaches that 'misuse after misuse' (מועל אחר מועל) applies only to an animal and to כלי שרת. רבי says instead that it applies to anything that cannot be redeemed. The גמרא shows that the משנה follows רבי נחמיה. A ברייתא has a תנא קמא who limits the rule to an animal, because the פסוק mentions איל האשם. רבי נחמיה adds כלי שרת by a קל וחומר: a vessel that makes its contents holy is surely holy itself. The גמרא then asks how רבי differs from the תנא קמא. רבא says they differ about donated wood, which רבי treats as a real קרבן, and רבא and רב פפא draw out results of that view. רב פפא gives a second answer: altar animals that became blemished and were slaughtered before redemption, where רבי says to bury them and חכמים say to redeem them. Finally, a new משנה begins: taking a stone or beam of הקדש is not מעילה.

steps.title: Benefit and damage must both reach a פרוטה in the same item
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person is not liable for מעילה unless he gets a פרוטה's worth of benefit and causes a פרוטה's worth of damage to one single item.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone got half a פרוטה of benefit and caused half a פרוטה of damage, or got a פרוטה of benefit from one item and caused a פרוטה of damage to another item, he did not commit מעילה. He is only liable when he gets a פרוטה of benefit and causes a פרוטה of damage to the same item.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the minimum for מעילה on an item that can be damaged: a full פרוטה of benefit and a full פרוטה of damage, both in one item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases fall short. In the first, neither the benefit nor the damage reaches a פרוטה. In the second, each one reaches a פרוטה, but they are split between two different items, so neither item has both together.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש (consecrated property) for personal use
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts in money matters
He got benefit from it
He damaged or reduced the item's value
He committed מעילה and is liable

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a person can add up a פרוטה of benefit from one item and a פרוטה of damage to another item. Both must happen to the same single item.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he derived benefit worth half a perutah
and caused damage worth half a perutah,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁנֶּהֱנָה בְּשָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בְּדָבָר אֶחָד
phrases.english: or if he derived benefit worth a perutah from one item
and caused damage worth a perutah to another item —
he has not committed misuse,
until he derives benefit worth a perutah
and causes damage worth a perutah, in one item.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נֶהֱנָה כְּבַחֲצִי פְרוּטָה וּפָגַם כַּחֲצִי פְרוּטָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעילה on a damageable item requires a פרוטה of benefit and a פרוטה of damage, both in the same item.

steps.title: Misuse after misuse applies only to an animal and service vessels
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that several people can each commit מעילה on the same item one after another, but only with an animal or a כלי שרת, and gives three examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: Misuse after misuse in הקדש applies only to an animal and to service vessels. How? If one person rode on a הקדש animal, then another rode, then another, all of them committed מעילה. If one drank from a gold cup of the מקדש, then another drank, then another, all committed מעילה. If one pulled wool from a חטאת, then another, then another, all committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a new rule, that some items can be misused again and again, and then illustrates it with three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when someone commits מעילה, the item leaves הקדש, so the next person to use it does not commit מעילה. An animal and a כלי שרת are the exception: they stay holy, so every new user is liable. The riding and wool cases show the animal, and the gold cup shows the כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: One person commits מעילה after another on the same item
Consecrated items (הקדש)
A service vessel used in the מקדש
How so? (introduces examples)
A sin offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the subject of the whole גמרא that follows, which asks whose opinion it is and why.

phrases.english: There is no misuse after misuse in consecrated items
except an animal and service vessels alone.
How so?
If one rode upon an animal,
phrases.notes: This means an animal set aside as a קרבן.

phrases.english: and another came and rode,
and another came and rode —
all of them have committed misuse.
If one drank from a gold cup,
and another came and drank,
and another came and drank —
all of them have committed misuse.
If one pulled wool from a sin offering,
and another came and pulled,
and another came and pulled —
all of them have committed misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹעֵל אַחַר מוֹעֵל בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין אֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה וּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New rule in the משנה, separate from the benefit-and-damage rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeated מעילה by several people applies only to a הקדש animal and to כלי שרת.

steps.title: רבי: anything that cannot be redeemed can be misused again and again
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives a broader rule: any הקדש item that has no redemption is subject to misuse after misuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: any item that cannot be redeemed is subject to misuse after misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with the list in the משנה and gives a general principle instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming specific items, רבי makes the rule depend on one feature: whether the item can be redeemed. If it can never be redeemed, it stays holy after being misused, so each new user commits מעילה again.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, taking an item out of הקדש by paying its value
It cannot be redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives a list (animal and כלי שרת), while רבי gives a principle (anything that cannot be redeemed).

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Any item that has no redemption —
is subject to misuse after misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ פִּדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion that broadens the rule of step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Misuse after misuse applies to any הקדש item that cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא holds the view that misuse after misuse applies to an animal and כלי שרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה's rule is. This sets up the next step, where it names him and brings a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points to the rule in step 2. Since other תנאים disagree about which items are included, the גמרא wants to know whose side the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose is it? (asking who the author is)
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose is it?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking whose opinion the משנה's list of 'animal and service vessels' follows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the author of the rule in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא authored the משנה's rule that misuse after misuse applies to an animal and כלי שרת

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is רבי נחמיה, and brings a ברייתא where the תנא קמא limits the rule to animals and רבי נחמיה includes כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is רבי נחמיה. As a ברייתא teaches: misuse after misuse applies only to an animal. רבי נחמיה says: an animal and service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי נחמיה as the author and proves it from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the first opinion includes only an animal. רבי נחמיה adds כלי שרת, which matches the משנה exactly. So the משנה follows רבי נחמיה, not the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An animal only

phrases.english: Our mishna is Rabbi Nechemya,
as it is taught: There is no misuse after misuse
except with an animal alone.
Rabbi Nechemya says:
An animal and service vessels.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who includes both an animal and כלי שרת, against the תנא קמא who includes only an animal.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: only an animal. רבי נחמיה (our משנה): an animal and כלי שרת.

steps.title: Why does the תנא קמא limit it to an animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the תנא קמא of the ברייתא, who excludes כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the first opinion in the ברייתא includes only an animal. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question looks at the narrower opinion. We need to know what source makes the תנא קמא leave out כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first opinion quoted in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning for limiting misuse after misuse to an animal only

steps.title: The פסוק about מעילה speaks of an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא holds that the topic is written about an animal, as the פסוק says 'with the ram of the guilt offering'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that it is written in the context of an animal, as it says: 'with the ram of the guilt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the תנא קמא's source: the פסוק about מעילה mentions an animal, the איל אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about מעילה (ויקרא 5:15–16) mention a ram brought as an אשם. The תנא קמא learns from this that misuse after misuse is tied to an animal, so he does not extend it to כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
In the context of an animal
The ram of the guilt offering

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא's source is the phrase 'איל האשם', which ties the topic to an animal.

phrases.english: He holds:
it is written in the context of an animal,
as it is written: “With the ram of the guilt offering.”

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns from 'איל האשם' that the topic is written about an animal, so misuse after misuse applies only to an animal.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's reasoning: a קל וחומר from the vessel's power to make things holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה answers the תנא קמא with a קל וחומר. A כלי שרת makes the things put inside it holy. So the vessel itself should surely be subject to misuse after misuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נחמיה would answer you with a קל וחומר: if the vessel brings other things into holiness, then surely the vessel itself has that holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives רבי נחמיה's reason for including כלי שרת, even though the פסוק speaks about an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא limited the rule to animals because the פסוק talks about a ram. רבי נחמיה argues from logic instead. Things placed in a כלי שרת become holy and are subject to misuse after misuse. So the vessel that gives them this holiness must surely have it too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one: if it is true there, it is surely true here
Holiness; the holy status of something given to the בית המקדש
All the more so

phrases.english: And Rabbi Neḥemya would say to you:
It is an a fortiori argument:
If it brings other things into their holiness,
phrases.notes: "It" is the כלי שרת, the service vessel. Things put into it become holy.

phrases.english: then the vessel itself, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, אָמַר לָךְ: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reasoning, after the תנא קמא's reason was given in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי נחמיה includes כלי שרת because of a קל וחומר: the vessel makes its contents holy, so it is surely holy itself
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two תנאים argue about method. One reads the rule narrowly from the פסוק, and the other widens it through logic.

steps.title: Isn't רבי's rule the same as the תנא קמא's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's line from the משנה. It then asks why רבי is shown as a separate opinion, since his rule seems to match the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: any item that has no redemption is subject to misuse after misuse, and so on. But that is just what the תנא קמא said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי's statement in the משנה. It challenges the statement as seemingly saying nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said that animals and כלי שרת, which cannot be redeemed, are subject to misuse after misuse. רבי's rule, "anything without redemption," seems to cover the same cases. If there is no difference, why is it listed as a separate view?

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about the law itself. The גמרא only wants to know what practical difference there is between רבי and the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Any item that is not subject to redemption,
there is, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the line in the משנה: there is misuse after misuse.

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנא קמא and רבי נחמיה debate back to רבי's line in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי's rule covers the same cases as the תנא קמא, there is no reason to record it as a separate opinion

steps.title: רבא: they disagree about wood
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the practical difference between רבי and the תנא קמא is donated wood for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by naming a case where the two views lead to different results: wood given to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lists specific items, such as an animal and כלי שרת. Wood is not on that list. But רבי's broad rule covers any holy item that cannot be redeemed. The next step shows that רבי considers wood a real קרבן, so wood would fall under his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Wood; logs donated for the fire on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rava said:
There is a difference between them: wood.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and the תנא קמא seem to say the same thing
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about donated wood, which רבי treats as a קרבן

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי holds that wood is a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי considers donated wood a real קרבן. It needs salt and waving like a מנחה. This supports רבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: someone who says "I take upon myself to bring wood" must bring at least two logs. רבי says: wood is a קרבן, so it needs salt and it needs waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for רבא's claim that רבי gives wood a special status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion only sets the minimum amount for a vow of wood. רבי goes further and calls wood a קרבן with the rules of a קרבן, salt and waving. This explains why wood falls under רבי's rule of misuse after misuse.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me": the words used to make a vow to bring something
Logs (cut pieces of wood)
An offering brought on the מזבח
Salt, which is put on offerings on the מזבח
Waving, a ritual done with certain offerings such as some מנחות

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
One who says: "It is upon me to bring wood"
may not bring fewer than two logs.
Rabbi says: Wood is an offering,
and it requires salt, and it requires waving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רבא's answer in step 10
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי and the תנא קמא differ about wood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי calls wood a קרבן that needs salt and waving
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, donated wood is a real קרבן. That is why it falls under his rule of misuse after misuse, while the תנא קמא does not include it.

steps.title: רבא: according to רבי, wood needs other wood
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out a striking result of רבי's view. Since wood is a קרבן, it needs other wood to burn it, like any other קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: according to רבי, wood needs wood.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has shown רבי treats wood as a קרבן, רבא draws out an unusual result of that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every קרבן is burned on wood from the מזבח. If the donated wood is itself a קרבן, then it also needs separate wood to be burned on. רבא is showing how far רבי's idea goes.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words (view) of
Require; need

phrases.english: Rava said: According to the statement of Rabbi,
wood requires wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a result from רבי's view in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי's view, donated wood is a קרבן, so other wood is needed to burn it

steps.title: רב פפא: according to רבי, wood needs קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds another result of רבי's view. Since wood is treated like a מנחה, a handful must be removed from it, like the קמיצה of a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: according to רבי, wood needs קמיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a second result to רבא's, showing again how fully רבי treats wood as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compared wood to a מנחה, since it needs salt and waving. רב פפא carries the comparison further: a מנחה needs קמיצה, so wood does too. This is a side remark about רבי's view of wood. The next step returns to the question from Step 9 with a second answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Need; require

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's broad rule (anything holy that cannot be redeemed) includes donated wood, because he treats wood as a full קרבן. רבא and רב פפא show how far this goes: it needs other wood to burn it, and it needs קמיצה.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said: According to the statement of Rabbi,
wood requires removal of a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second result alongside רבא's in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי's view, donated wood needs קמיצה like a מנחה

steps.title: רב פפא's alternate difference: blemished altar animals that were slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer from רבא. The practical difference between רבי and the תנא קמא is altar animals that became blemished and were slaughtered before they were redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If animals set aside for the מזבח were unblemished, then became blemished, and someone wrongly slaughtered them, that is where רבי and the תנא קמא differ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from Step 9 and gives a second answer, this time from רב פפא. He names a different case where רבי and the תנא קמא would disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the difference was donated wood. רב פפא points to a different case: consecrated animals that got a מום and were slaughtered before being redeemed. The next step will show that רבי and חכמים really do argue about exactly this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside to be brought on the altar
Unblemished, fit to be a קרבן
Animals with a blemish, which can no longer be offered
He did wrong and slaughtered them (before redeeming them)

steps.confusionAlert: This רב פפא is not adding to his own statement in Step 13. He is giving a new answer to the question from Step 9, as an alternative to רבא's answer about wood.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
animals consecrated for the altar that were unblemished
and they became blemished
and someone transgressed and slaughtered them
phrases.notes: The wrong was slaughtering them before they were redeemed. A blemished animal is supposed to be redeemed first.

phrases.english: there is a difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 9's question, parallel to רבא's answer in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different practical case where the two opinions disagree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's rule seemed the same as the תנא קמא's, so there seemed to be no reason to list it separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about blemished altar animals that were slaughtered before redemption.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי and חכמים argue about this case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that in this very case, רבי says the animals must be buried, while חכמים say they can be redeemed. This supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And indeed a ברייתא teaches: If altar animals were unblemished, became blemished, and someone slaughtered them, רבי says they must be buried, and חכמים say they can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב פפא. It shows a real disagreement in exactly the case he named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says the slaughtered animals can no longer be redeemed, so they must be buried. That means they keep their holiness itself and cannot be turned into money. חכמים say they can still be redeemed, which fits the תנא קמא's view, so this is a real difference between the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be buried, since no one may benefit from them
They can be redeemed, so the holiness moves onto money

steps.confusionAlert: Here וְהָתַנְיָא does not open a challenge. It means "and indeed it is taught," and it supports רב פפא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב פפא did not make up the case. There is a known disagreement that lines up with the two opinions in the משנה.

phrases.english: And indeed it is taught in a baraita:
animals consecrated for the altar that were unblemished,
and they became blemished,
and someone transgressed and slaughtered them,
Rabbi says: they must be buried,
and the Rabbis say: they should be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's answer from Step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that רבי and the תנא קמא differ about slaughtered blemished altar animals
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי rules the animals must be buried and חכמים rule they can be redeemed
steps.whatToRemember: The question from Step 9 has two answers. רבא says the difference is donated wood (Step 10). רב פפא says it is blemished altar animals slaughtered before redemption, where רבי says bury them and חכמים say redeem them.

steps.title: New משנה: taking a stone or beam of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Someone who takes a stone or a beam that belongs to הקדש has not committed מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone took a stone or a beam of הקדש, he has not committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion of the previous משנה is finished, and a new משנה starts. It deals with someone who takes a building item, a stone or a beam, that belongs to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking הקדש property here is not enough to make the person guilty of מעילה. This opens a new topic: when exactly does handling הקדש property count as מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
